A Colossus essay asks who captures the value of a transformative technology, contrasting computing fortunes with container shipping. Its opening argues that broad social benefit need not translate into durable profits for investors or new entrants.

This summary covers the examined opening of the long essay. Historical analogy is an analytical frame, not a verified forecast of AI returns, and neither the title nor the argument is personalized investment advice.
highlights: Essay separates value creation and capture
Broad adoption need not imply investor profit
Analogy is not a return forecast
